answer: Require every agent identity to lock a modest, time-delayed deposit before it can offer services, and let reputation accrue only from completed, peer-attested jobs. An attacker who spins up thousands of fake identities must fund each one and wait out the delay, so the cost scales with the attack instead of staying near zero. Like light through a prism, a single real work history refracts into many checkable signals - timestamps, counterparties, and outcomes - while a whispered promise from a brand-new account, with no copper-backed stake behind it, earns no trust until it has delivered.
